title: async and Promises

outcomes.can: Distinguish the promise from its resolved value and identify where to catch rejection.

intro: A promise represents a result that may arrive later. A fulfilled promise carries a value and a rejected one carries a reason. An async function always returns a promise. Inside it, await obtains the fulfilled value or throws the rejection where you awaited it. A local async fixture can return known data with no network or timer.

steps.title: Trace the example
steps.text: The first await gets the text from readName. Only after that does the concatenation produce Hello Jo. Await a possibly rejected reader inside try to let its catch handle the failure. Returning a promise directly from inside try can move its rejection past that catch.
